# Assessment source restrictions — Debate 286

Exact motion: Did Jesus fulfill prophecy? Samuel Nesan is pro; Matt Dillahunty is con. Nesan argues Jesus fulfilled part of the Old Testament’s predictions within a unified covenant/redemption narrative; he explicitly does not claim all prophecies have already been fulfilled. Dillahunty generally argues fulfillment is not demonstrable, rather than proving no fulfillment could ever occur. His narrower rebuttal distinguishes reasonable confidence from certainty. Preserve these actual burdens.

The complete canonical source has events 0–5033. Retain only events 6–1819, approximately 0:11.679–1:02:30.960. The source envelope extends to 3:08:01 solely for exclusion accounting. Everything from 1:02:30.960 onward is excluded: audience Q&A, both speakers’ answers and dependent replies, courtesy farewells, music, and the host-only after-show. No separate formal closing speeches occur. Do not penalize either person for that format. Full excluded text is supplied for boundary/completeness review, never evidence, credit, penalty, quotation, response target, inferred concession or absence inference.

Formal phase anchors (inclusive canonical indices): Nesan opening 6–258; Dillahunty opening 263–561; Nesan rebuttal 579–722; Dillahunty rebuttal 726–831; Nesan-led cross-examination 841–1118; Dillahunty-led cross-examination 1132–1251; brief Nesan cross-examination continuation 1255–1273; mutually accepted open discussion from approximately 1283–1819. Questions and answers within cross-examination alternate: the questioner does not own every intervening statement. Ordinary moderator timing/logistics, sound checks, promotions and quoted audience praise are unscored. Caption timings overlap at boundaries; preserve literal event text and avoid assigning carry-over words to the wrong speaker.

Six source clips were transcribed once with gpt-4o-mini-transcribe and compared with the canonical captions. They corroborate Nesan’s partial-fulfillment qualification, named speaker handoffs, Dillahunty’s certainty/reasonableness distinction, the Isaiah 53 exchange, and the specific-prophecy/context/magic-trick debate. This is an independent audio-derived text cross-check, not direct listening or speaker diarization. Source lock records exact clips, successful outputs, costs and limitations. Any materially unresolved wording or ownership must still be flagged below high; never force high confidence to avoid verification.

Source-specific restrictions and qualifications:
- Around 11:03–11:08, a mundane-biography sentence is broken in both canonical captions and the independent transcription. Do not invent the missing claim or count the gap as a weakness. Independently complete surrounding claims remain eligible.
- Nesan’s “not all prophecies” opening qualification and his concession that the Moriah/Isaac correspondence is not conclusive by itself must remain visible in assessments of his cumulative argument.
- Dillahunty explicitly says he is not a mythicist. Do not label his methodological criticism as a positive Jesus-never-existed claim. He clarifies certainty versus reasonable confidence in his rebuttal and permits reasonable understanding of authorial intent at 52:23–52:35.
- The pre-show magic trick is described by both participants, but its performance is absent. Assess the analogy and reported demonstration as stated, not an independently verified supernatural or magical achievement.
- Nesan says he accepts specificity while contesting its threshold, universal interpretation, and the distinction between covenant promises and predictions. Do not erase those replies by asserting he simply rejects specificity.
- Nesan’s early historical-witness names are recognition-corrupted; do not quote corrupted names or infer mistakes from their spelling. Evaluate the presented historical reasoning, with its own evidence limitations.
- At 38:21–38:25 Dillahunty explicitly corrects Isaiah to Abraham. Preserve the correction rather than treating the initial name slip as a settled premise. Around 39:02 the moderator identifies a connection interruption and requests a repeat; the complete 39:11 restatement controls, with no missing-reply inference from the damaged earlier phrase.
- The 41:06 contextual answer must be read with Nesan’s 42:18 clarification that he considers many prophecies specific and his named Isaiah 53/Genesis 22 examples. Do not turn inability to isolate one context-free passage into a concession that none is specific.
- In the testimony/magic-trick exchange, Nesan starts an interrupted qualification “Unless there’s”. Do not reconstruct its absent completion or claim the interruption proves he accepts all testimony unconditionally. The separately stated trust analogy remains assessable at its actual scope.
- Short connection failures recur near 45:58 and 53:02. Textual repetitions recover complete surrounding arguments, but broken phrases themselves cannot supply a penalty, alleged evasion or quotation.
- At 55 minutes Nesan’s canonical “Luke 44:44” is recognition corruption: the independent audio-derived transcript gives Luke 24:44–48. The canonical text remains unchanged. Dillahunty’s explicit correction from 21 to 24 is preserved separately. Neither corrupted numerals nor cross-talk are an independent argumentative defect.
- Nesan expressly disclaims using Hosea 6 as a prophecy argument. Dillahunty’s objection to that passage may be assessed as his own challenge, but never credited as a refutation of a premise Nesan adopted.
- Dillahunty’s discussion of Jesus’s sexuality is a hypothetical comparison of interpretive standards, not established biography. Nesan’s cultural-context reply and the ensuing law/fulfillment exchange belong to their actual speakers. Distinguish possibility, comparative interpretive warrant and confident historical assertion.
- Both speakers say the final law discussion is outside prophecy; preserve the relevance qualification while assessing any selected methodological significance. Excluded Q&A must not rescue, refute or supplement either case.

Featured quote eligibility requires a complete exact 3–18 word thought, with meaning-changing qualification retained. At least one such source span per side must be secured before inventory freeze. When a sentence cannot fit, select another complete thought; do not fabricate completion or rely on explanatory text to complete the quote.
